text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - Bunds, futures briefly fall to session lows in tight range trade on U.S. jobs data. Rising dollar underpins market as U.S. debt begins recovering after initial drop. The September Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.89, up 0.38 from Thursday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilts locked in a dramatic 21/32 gain on Friday after BOE raised rates by 25 bps. But traders said with host of data due next week, some of it expected strong, market may be subject to hefty profittaking. Short stg back months also seen overvalued. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 113-24/32, up 20/32 from Thursday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures close higher but off day's highs while the franc weakened ahead of meeting of EU finance ministers Sunday evening, Monday which European markets will be closely watching for signs of how France's new left-wing government behaves on European policy. June PIBOR futures end flat after trading in tight range all day. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 129.40 up 0.14 from Thursday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian Btp bond futures slid at the close, following Spanish Bonos, while the the 10-year Btp bond spread over the benchmark bund widened and the lira eased against the mark amid EMU uncertainty ahead of Sunday's Ecofin meeting. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 129.60 down 0.20 from Thursday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries stay lower, steady in mid-morning trading. Overall strong tone to May employment report pressures market. Short end hit most, as players raise odds for July rate hike. 2-30 year yield curve flattens to 65 bps, lowest since May 19. Large hedge fund sold $800 million in 2-year notes. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 110-30/32, up 17/32 from Thursday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.83 percent.

JAPAN - Key September 10-year Japanese goverment bonds (JGB) futures contract ended quiet Tokyo day higher on buying of cash bonds in expectation that 190th bond will soon become benchmark. Pre-weekend book-squaring from traders also detected as market waits for U.S. employment data later today.In after hours trading the September future on LIFFE was trading at 122.91, up 0.10 from Thursday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market ended a hectic week of issuance with the launch of Moldova's debut bond. Venezuela's planned 10-year bond is due early next week. Fannie Mae launched the largest global New Zealand dollar bond. Early in the session France's CCCI set a $750 million 7-year FRN.
